2609.14121.title: Semantic Knowledge Technologies: what the Semantic Web lost sight of, and what it never had
2609.14121.paper_summary: The Semantic Web set out to give information a machine-interpretable form so that software could integrate and reason over it. Its standards became scientific knowledge infrastructure, but the machine competence it promised did not follow, and the systems now answering questions over scientific knowledge are language models holding no inspectable account of what they know. This paper argues the original goal was right and the technical programme incomplete, states what is missing, and names the extended programme Semantic Knowledge Technologies: the same technical core carried out of its web-publishing origin and applied to knowledge wherever held. The diagnosis is that the standards formalised truth while omitting three things: the conditions under which a claim holds, the operations its terms permit, and any account of what a base covers. Without conditions, contradiction and applicability cannot be judged; without operational grounding, holding a statement confers no ability; without declared coverage, a system cannot recognise the boundary of its own content, which under the open-world assumption cannot be inferred. The paper fixes the word understanding to five measurable tests (check, connect, derive, act, delimit) and sets out a seven-layer architecture in which the first three layers are enabling and the rest the cognitive capabilities they make possible. It then defines three terms the programme implies: Large Knowledge Model, a model whose unit of output is a reference to an addressable claim, not a token; SLKM, the knowledge base an agent builds for itself from declared sources; and Semantic Artificial General Intelligence, stated as a falsifiable position about necessary conditions, not a system. A graded ladder replaces the untestable word general. It is offered as a research agenda, with its weakest points and refutation condition named.
2609.14121.paper_summary_zh: 語義網旨在為信息提供機器可解釋的形式，以便軟件能夠整合並推理其上。它的標準成為科學知識基礎設施，但其所承諾的機器能力並未實現，而如今回答科學知識問題的系統是沒有可檢查的知識來源的語言模型。本文主張最初的目標是正確的，技術方案是不完整的，指出了缺失的部分，並命名擴展方案為語義知識技術：同樣的技術核心從其網頁發布的起源中延伸出來，並應用於各種知識。診斷結果是，標準形式化了真理，但忽略了三件事：一個主張成立的條件、其術語允許的操作，以及基礎所涵蓋的任何說明。沒有條件，就無法判斷矛盾和適用性；沒有操作基礎，持有一個陳述不會賦予任何能力；沒有明確的覆蓋範圍，系統無法識別其自身內容的邊界，而在開放世界假設下，這是無法推斷的。本文將“理解”一詞固定為五個可測試的標準（檢查、連接、推導、行動、界定），並提出一個七層架構，其中前三層是使能層，其餘則是它們所使能的認知能力。然後定義了該方案所暗示的三個術語：大型知識模型，一個其輸出單位是對可尋址主張的引用，而不是標記的模型；SLKM，代理從已聲明來源為自己構建的知識庫；以及語義人工通用智能，表述為關於必要條件的可反駁立場，而不是一個系統。一個分級梯度取代了不可測試的“通用”一詞。這被提出作為一個研究議程，並命名了其最弱的點和反駁條件。
2609.14121.author: Achille Zappa et.al.
